programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: International chain campus — Valencia campus of a private US college (Berklee, Boston). VERIFIED on the official accreditation page: Berklee Valencia is a Spanish 'Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música', 'officially recognized by Resolution of the General Director of Universities, Higher Studies and Sciences no. 6844, dated August 8, 2012.'
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.M.) — a UNITED STATES degree. VERIFIED: it is NOT a Spanish 'Máster Universitario Oficial' and NOT a Spanish título propio. Berklee's own accreditation page states verbatim: 'All Berklee degrees are accredited by the New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE) in the United States' and then, separately, 'The Master of Arts in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games are accredited in Spain, in collaboration with the Universidad Politécnica de Valencia.' MPTI is NOT in that list. Cross-check confirms it: the MPTI programme and courses pages quote credits only in the US system (32–38 credits) and carry NO ECTS figure and NO RUCT code, whereas the SFTV page states '60 ECTS' and 'RUCT código 4313419'. The absence is decisive.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL in the USA / NOT a Spanish official degree. Accrediting body: New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), USA. VERIFIED by direct comparison of the MPTI and SFTV pages: SFTV publishes a RUCT code and ECTS, MPTI publishes neither. In practice: a genuine, respected US master's degree, but it does not appear in Spain's RUCT register of official degrees, so it does not by itself give access to a Spanish doctorate or to title-dependent public-sector posts without a separate homologación/equivalencia procedure. What matters for the visa is the INSTITUTION's authorisation, which is confirmed.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Berklee Valencia is an officially authorised Spanish higher-education centre (Resolution 6844, 8 Aug 2012, verified on the accreditation page) and enrols non-EU students full-time, on campus, for three consecutive semesters. It issues the admission letter required for the Spanish type-D student visa. This is the most visa-reliable private option in this batch.
programs.focus: Music production, electronic music production and performance, DJing, audio engineering, sound design, music video, interactive media, artist/producer career development.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module-by-module from the official courses page. Core Module: Audio Engineering (3 cr), Studio Music Production (2 cr), Music Video Production (3 cr), Interactive Media (2 cr), Electronic Music Production and Performance (3 cr), Career Preparation (1 cr), Proficiencies (0 cr). Final Project Module: three MPTI Seminars (2 cr each) plus three Culminating Experience courses (2, 2 and 4 cr). Elective Module: minimum 4 credits chosen from audio engineering, production, theory, DJing, video, interactive media or electronic music. Additional optional courses (research, rhythm studies, ensembles, private instruction) do NOT count toward the degree. Optional 4th-semester Graduate Internship. DJing is a named elective area — verified, not inferred.
programs.durationEcts: One full academic year — 'a consecutive fall, spring, and summer' (three semesters). Total Minimum Required Credits: 32, or 33 with internship. Total Maximum Allowed Credits: 37, or 38 with internship. US credit system. NO ECTS equivalence is published for MPTI — verified absence, and this is itself the accreditation signal.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (fall start). Curriculum published for the 2026–2027 academic year.
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD 50,430 — VERIFIED on the official graduate tuition page for 2026/2027. Per-credit rate USD 1,615. Because the master is one year, this is also the whole-programme figure. Non-EU students pay the same as everyone else; Berklee publishes a single rate.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD 50,430 total tuition for the whole programme, academic year 2026/2027. VERIFIED at https://valencia.berklee.edu/tuition-fees-payment/tuition-and-related-costs-for-graduate-programs
programs.otherFees: ALL VERIFIED on the official 2026/2027 graduate tuition page: Application fee USD 150 (waived for Berklee alumni); non-refundable Tuition Deposit USD 2,500; Comprehensive Fee USD 1,600 (mandatory for all students — it covers registration into the Spanish educational system and compulsory health insurance among other services); required Software Bundle for MPTI USD 800 (purchased directly from Berklee). CORRECTION CONFIRMED: the Professional Recording Services Fee of USD 2,990 applies to the Scoring programme ONLY and is NOT charged to MPTI. Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP): students 'must accept enrollment in Berklee's Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP) or submit a waiver request' — standalone amount NOT published, UNVERIFIED (note the comprehensive fee is stated to include compulsory health insurance, so double-counting is a risk). Third-party credential evaluation of non-US transcripts is required and carries an external cost — amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: VERIFIED: required Software Bundle USD 800 for MPTI, purchased directly from Berklee. Laptop estimated at USD 3,000 in Berklee's own indirect-cost table, annotated 'may be waived' (i.e. if he already owns a suitable machine — as a software-engineering graduate he almost certainly does, so treat this as avoidable). Studios, consoles and hardware are provided on campus.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Direct cost billed by the college, all figures verified: USD 50,430 tuition + 1,600 comprehensive fee + 800 software + 150 application = USD 52,980 (the 2,500 deposit is credited against tuition, not additional). Adding Berklee's own published indirect estimates — housing USD 10,000–12,000, books USD 300–800, local transport USD 300–600, personal USD 1,000 — gives a realistic all-in first year of approximately USD 65,000–68,000 WITHOUT the laptop, or USD 68,000–71,000 with it (roughly EUR 60,000–66,000 at mid-2026 rates). Add credential evaluation and any SHIP premium. This is by far the most expensive option in this batch — roughly 12–16x the UCAM alternative.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED exact wording from the official entrance-requirements page: 'Applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music while demonstrating technological proficiency, musical excellence in performance and/or composition, leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity, and promise of great achievement in their area of study.' Ideal candidates demonstrate: 'Excellent musicianship; Facility with technology; Success in both artistic and academic settings; A strong work ethic, including prior accomplishment; and The motivation to make massive progress in one year.' Application package (verified): online application + USD 150 fee, statement of purpose 'between 400 and 500 words' in English, résumé/CV in English, ONE letter of recommendation (from a professional, not a peer), official transcripts with third-party credential evaluation for non-US/Canada qualifications.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, conditionally. VERIFIED published wording: 'Applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music. Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship.' A BSc in Software Engineering is therefore an acceptable degree — but the entire burden shifts to demonstrated musicianship and production output. His software background maps directly onto the separately-listed criterion 'facility with technology', which is a genuine and unusual asset here.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW FULLY VERIFIED (previously marked unverified — corrected). MPTI applicants must submit: (1) a self-produced video, maximum three minutes, describing 'three projects you feel passionate about, and that you would like to develop as part of your Culminating Experience (thesis) project' — with the explicit constraint 'you should not talk about projects that you have already completed'; (2) 'Three recorded musical projects, audio or video files of your work, including a short description of your role in each project'; (3) optionally, the corresponding musical scores if available. All materials must be organised 'in one PDF document with all links properly embedded and sections clearly labeled'. This is a concrete, buildable target: three finished tracks plus a forward-looking three-minute pitch video. He can start today.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition for MPTI — auditions apply to the Contemporary Performance programme only. Selected applicants are invited to an INTERVIEW.
programs.englishTest: IELTS IS ACCEPTED, AND THE MINIMUM IS NOW VERIFIED — THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST CORRECTION IN THIS BATCH. Berklee Valencia publishes two tiers: Contemporary Performance requires Duolingo 110 / TOEFL iBT 80 (pre-Jan-2026 scale) / IELTS 6.5. ALL OTHER PROGRAMMES, INCLUDING MPTI, REQUIRE Duolingo 130 / TOEFL iBT 100 / IELTS 7.5. IELTS 7.5 is a demanding band — well above the 6.0–6.5 typical of European master's entry. He has not sat IELTS yet. This should be treated as a hard gate and planned for now: it realistically needs months of preparation, and the test must be in hand before the November 2026 / January 2027 deadlines. The requirement applies only if English is not his first language; a waiver may apply if his bachelor's was taught and examined in English — confirm his SMU MedTech medium of instruction with admissions in writing, because that waiver could remove the gate entirely.
programs.applicationOpens: Applications open in the autumn preceding entry (the Early Action deadline is 1 November). Exact 2027-entry opening date not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: VERIFIED as recurring annual dates on the official deadlines page, with no entry year attached (so they are the standing pattern): Early Action — application 1 November, scholarship 15 November, decisions issued by 15 December. Regular Action — application 15 January, scholarship 1 February, decisions by 15 March. Extended Action — application 10 March, scholarship 10 March, decisions by 20 April. programs.scholarships: VERIFIED against the official graduate scholarships page. Applicable to him: Berklee General Scholarship — all master's applicants, amount varies, deadline 15 Nov (early) or 1 Feb (regular). Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — 'Up to 50 percent of the tuition', all graduate programmes, 'Up to four awardees per academic year', for 'demonstrated leadership or support for historically underrepresented or culturally diverse communities'; CORRECTION: the deadline is 1 FEBRUARY ONLY, not 15 November — so applying Early Action does not advance this one. Realistic ceiling for him: the Diversity Scholarship at up to 50%, competing for one of four awards campus-wide.

programs.facilities: Campus inside the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía opera house, Valencia. Recording studios and technology labs; professional software stack taught across the curriculum (Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere).

programs.verificationNotes: Verified across five official pages: the MPTI programme page, the MPTI courses page, the graduate tuition and related costs page (2026/2027), the graduate entrance-requirements page, the how-to-apply page, the application-deadlines page, the graduate scholarships page, and the accreditation page. STILL UNVERIFIED: SHIP health-insurance amount, credential-evaluation cost, graduate instalment terms, exact 2027-cycle opening date.
programs.recommendation: The best CONTENT fit in this batch for an aspiring international DJ/producer — Electronic Music Production and Performance is a required core course and DJing is a named elective area, verified in the official course list, not marketing copy. The network and the brand are real. But three hard facts must govern the decision. (1) COST: roughly USD 65,000–71,000 all-in for one year, with no need-based aid route published for international students. That is irreconcilable with 'budget-sensitive' unless he wins a large award, and the only award realistically open to him is the Diversity Scholarship at up to 50%, capped at four recipients campus-wide. (2) TWO GATES HE HAS NOT CLEARED: IELTS 7.5 — now verified, and a high band he has not yet attempted; and the published standard 'a high degree of musicianship', against which he brings no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio work. The portfolio spec is at least now precise and achievable: three finished, well-produced tracks with a clear account of his role in each, plus a three-minute video pitching three UNBUILT projects. Working backwards from a 1 Nov 2026 Early Action deadline, he has roughly twelve months — enough, but only if he starts now and treats it as the priority. (3) The degree is a US master, not a Spanish official title — fine for industry, a real limitation if he ever wants a Spanish PhD or a title-dependent role. VERDICT: apply, aim for Early Action for the General Scholarship and target the Diversity Scholarship at the 1 February deadline, but treat this as the aspirational option. Do not commit self-pay funds without an award of 40%+, and keep a cheaper Spanish option live in parallel.

programs.program: Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games (SFTV)

programs.qualification: DUAL AWARD, NOW POSITIVELY VERIFIED. A US Master of Music (M.M.) AND a Spanish official Máster Universitario. Berklee's accreditation page states: 'The Master of Arts in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the Master of Music in Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games are accredited in Spain, in collaboration with the Universidad Politécnica de Valencia.' The programme page confirms the mechanics: 'RUCT código 4313419', 60 ECTS, 'valid throughout the European Higher Education Area (EHEA)'. programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL IN BOTH SYSTEMS — the strongest legal standing of any programme in this batch. NECHE (USA) plus a Spanish Máster Universitario Oficial registered in RUCT under code 4313419, delivered in affiliation with Universitat Politècnica de València. In practice: 60 ECTS, valid across the EHEA, valid for PhD entry, and unambiguous for visa and title-recognition purposes. This is emphatically NOT a título propio.
programs.visaEligible: Yes, unambiguously. Same authorised centre as MPTI, plus registration in RUCT as an official Spanish Máster Universitario through UPV — which removes any residual consular doubt. The cleanest visa position in this batch.
programs.focus: Composition and scoring for film, television and video games; orchestration; conducting; recording and mixing of score with live musicians; game-audio work.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED structure from the official programme page: Core Module — visual media languages, orchestral techniques, visual media technology and recording, career seminar. Final Project Module — directed studies plus culminating experience. Elective Module — one elective course. Score recording sessions with professional musicians are funded by the dedicated recording-services fee.
programs.durationEcts: One academic year, three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer; summer term 6–7 weeks). VERIFIED: 39–40 US credits, stated as 60 ECTS. Intake capped at 30 students annually on the Berklee page (UPV's 2026/27 offer lists 40 official places).
programs.language: English — 'all classes are taught in English' (verified).
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (fall start).
programs.tuitionPerYear: USD 50,430 for 2026/2027 — VERIFIED, same graduate tuition as MPTI.
programs.tuitionTotal: USD 50,430 total tuition for the whole programme, academic year 2026/2027. Non-EU students pay the same rate.
programs.otherFees: ALL VERIFIED on the official 2026/2027 graduate tuition page: Application fee USD 150; non-refundable Tuition Deposit USD 2,500; Comprehensive Fee USD 1,600; Professional Recording Services Fee USD 2,990 — explicitly and exclusively 'Scoring for Film, Television, and Video Games only', described as contributing 'to a fraction of the extraordinary studio and recording expenses unique to the scoring program'; required Software Bundle USD 700 for the Scoring programme (note: LOWER than MPTI's USD 800). With Berklee's published indirect estimates (housing 10,000–12,000, books 300–800, transport 300–600, personal 1,000) the all-in first year is approximately USD 68,000–71,000 without a laptop purchase, or up to USD 74,000 with it. programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED, AND STRICTER THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Ideal candidates must 'Demonstrate a strong compositional foundation from their studies and/or professional experience; Possess the ability to notate one's ideas competently, follow an orchestral score, and conceive material in an orchestral context; and Exhibit passion for musical storytelling and a demonstrated aptitude for visual music.'
programs.acceptsNonMusic: EFFECTIVELY NO — CORRECTION. The verified wording is mandatory, not preferential: 'Applicants are required to hold a bachelor's degree in music composition, electronic music production, or film scoring.' A BSc in Software Engineering does not satisfy this on its face. On top of the degree bar, applicants must be able to 'notate one's ideas competently, follow an orchestral score, and conceive material in an orchestral context' — score-reading and orchestral literacy he does not have and could not credibly acquire by autumn 2026. This is the hardest entry in the batch for his specific profile.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED. Required: (1) a self-produced introductory video, maximum three minutes; (2) 'Three video files of original compositions for picture. Berklee does provide a workaround for the picture requirement: applicants without film-scoring experience 'may extract clips from existing films and television shows via a number of available applications, import them to your music sequencing program, and create original compositions for the purposes of this application.' Applicable in principle: Berklee General Scholarship (amount varies, 15 Nov / 1 Feb) and the Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship (up to 50% of tuition, up to four awardees per year, deadline 1 February). programs.verificationNotes: Verified on the official programme page, the accreditation page, the entrance-requirements page, the how-to-apply page, the deadlines page, the scholarships page, the 2026/2027 tuition page, and cross-checked against UPV's published 2026/2027 master's places offer. programs.recommendation: AVOID — for fit, not quality. On paper this is the best-credentialled programme in the batch: a real Spanish Máster Universitario Oficial (RUCT 4313419, 60 ECTS) stacked on top of a US Master of Music, with the cleanest possible visa position. But it is the wrong instrument for him on two counts, and the second is disqualifying. First, it is composition-for-picture — orchestration, notation, conducting, scoring stages — not DJing, not electronic production, not club music. It does not serve his stated goal. Second, and decisively, the entry bar is now verified as mandatory: applicants are REQUIRED to hold a bachelor's in music composition, electronic music production or film scoring, and must be able to notate ideas, read an orchestral score and think orchestrally. He has none of that and cannot acquire it by autumn 2026. The mandatory portfolio of three original compositions to picture WITH written scores makes the gap concrete. It is also the most expensive option here — USD 55,870 in direct college costs because of the USD 2,990 recording-services fee, approaching USD 74,000 all-in. Listed for completeness and because it usefully proves that Berklee Valencia CAN deliver a Spanish official degree (which is exactly what MPTI does not). Skip it unless his ambitions genuinely shift to film and game scoring, in which case it becomes a multi-year plan, not a 2027 one.

programs.qualification: MÁSTER UNIVERSITARIO OFICIAL — VERIFIED. The official programme page states the status is 'Oficial' and that the degree certificate is issued by the Ministry of Education. 60 ECTS. This is an official Spanish degree, NOT a título propio.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL. programs.recommendation: The strongest DEGREE in this batch and the weakest fit for his stated goal — and the trade-off is worth taking seriously rather than dismissing. On the plus side: it is a genuine Máster Universitario Oficial, 60 ECTS, taught entirely in English, at a serious private university, with a clean visa path, real published scholarships (up to 50% on GPA alone), NO portfolio requirement and NO musicianship test. It is the one programme here where his BSc is an asset rather than a liability and where his complete absence of music credentials costs him nothing. The verified IELTS bar is also almost certainly lower than Berklee's 7.5, though it is not published. On the minus side: it will not make him a DJ or a producer. It is noise control, vibration management and signal processing for automotive, aerospace, rail and construction — the entertainment sector is one application area among six. Three blockers must be resolved before it can even be costed: (1) SOFTWARE ENGINEERING IS NOT ON THE PUBLISHED ADMISSIONS LIST — get written confirmation it qualifies, or the rest is moot; (2) TUITION IS NOT PUBLISHED ANYWHERE — he cannot compare this against Berklee or UCAM until he has the number in writing; (3) the English requirement is unpublished. All three are answered by one email to Sardor Abdullaev or Iona Marie Lafont Amado. Recommend it only under a specific strategy: 'get to Barcelona on a real, fundable, visa-safe technical degree in English, and build the music career on the side in one of Europe's best electronic-music cities.' Given his profile and budget sensitivity that is a genuinely defensible plan — but he should choose it with his eyes open, not mistake it for a music production master.

programs.program: Máster de Formación Permanente en Producción Musical (semipresencial)
programs.institution: UCAM — Universidad Católica San Antonio de Murcia
programs.institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Murcia). The institution itself is a fully recognised Spanish private university.
programs.qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — VERIFIED. Specifically a 'Máster de Formación Permanente en Producción Musical Semipresencial', 60 ECTS. This is UCAM's OWN diploma. It is NOT a Máster Universitario Oficial, it does not appear in the RUCT register of official degrees, and it does not give direct access to a Spanish doctorate. THIS IS EXACTLY THE TRAP THE SPANISH PRIVATE SECTOR IS KNOWN FOR — the word 'Máster' in the title does not make it an official degree.
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL as a degree. It is a título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente issued by UCAM under its own authority. The INSTITUTION is legitimate and recognised (UCAM is a real Spanish private university), but THIS AWARD is not ANECA-verified and is not an official master. In practice: a credible university-branded certificate with genuine industry weight and a real Steinberg Cubase professional certification attached — but legally a certificate, not a degree. He must not describe it as a master's degree on a CV in a jurisdiction that distinguishes the two.
programs.visaEligible: PROBABLY, BUT UNVERIFIED AND GENUINELY RISKY — DO NOT ASSUME. Spanish student visas require full-time study at an authorised centre. UCAM qualifies as an authorised centre, but the modality is confirmed SEMIPRESENCIAL (blended). Consulates routinely refuse, shorten or downgrade visa applications for programmes that are not full-time face-to-face, and a título propio adds no help. He must obtain written confirmation from UCAM's international office, naming this specific programme, that it supports a type-D student visa and residence permit for a Tunisian national — BEFORE paying the EUR 235 pre-enrolment fee. If the answer is no, the programme is worthless to him as a relocation route regardless of how good the content is.
programs.focus: Music production, composition techniques, artistic development, recording, mixing and mastering.

programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, one academic year. Verified.
programs.language: Spanish — VERIFIED. This is a hard blocker unless his Spanish is strong. No English-language option exists.
programs.intakes: One intake per academic year. The programme page does not publish a start date — UNVERIFIED; UCAM postgraduate courses conventionally begin in October. Confirm the 2027 date with admissions.

programs.tuitionTotal: EUR 3,900 total tuition for the whole 60-ECTS programme. Verified for the currently advertised edition — confirm the figure for the 2027/2028 edition, as UCAM revises fees annually.
programs.otherFees: VERIFIED on the official page: pre-enrolment fee EUR 235 (non-refundable); school insurance EUR 59.12. No other institutional fees are published. That is an unusually clean and transparent fee structure by the standards of this sector.

programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 4,194.12 in institutional costs (3,900 + 235 + 59.12) — every component verified. programs.recommendation: The best VALUE in this batch by an enormous margin, and the decision hinges entirely on one unanswered question. For EUR 4,194.12 all-in — every euro verified — he gets a 60-ECTS university-branded music production programme with Sony Music España involvement, named Spanish electronic producers teaching masterclasses, and an official Steinberg Cubase certification. His software-engineering degree is EXPLICITLY listed as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, and no IELTS is needed. Compare that with Berklee: he would pay roughly twelve to sixteen times as much and face an IELTS 7.5 gate and a musicianship bar he currently cannot clear. But three caveats must be resolved in order, and the first is decisive. (1) THE VISA. It is semipresencial, and this is precisely the format Spanish consulates refuse. If the answer is no, this programme cannot relocate him and its value collapses to zero for his stated purpose. (2) THE LANGUAGE. Teaching is entirely in Spanish, with no English track. If his Spanish is not already functional, twelve months of language work must run in parallel — which is still cheaper and more achievable than IELTS 7.5 plus USD 65,000. (3) THE AWARD. It is a título propio, legally a certificate, not an official degree — fine for an industry career where the Cubase certification and the Sony connection carry more weight than the parchment, but useless if he ever wants a Spanish PhD or a title-dependent role. If the visa answer comes back yes and his Spanish holds up, this is the highest return-on-euro option available to him in Spain and should be the pragmatic core of his plan, with Berklee as the aspirational stretch.

programs.entryRequirements: University degree or equivalent, or one being obtained by the end of 2025/2026; minimum B1.2 in English or Italian. Non-EU applicants must pre-enrol on the UniversItaly platform with passport, diploma, transcripts and language certificate, and must supply a 'dichiarazione di valore' from the Italian diplomatic mission or CIMEA comparability attestations.

programs.tuitionPerYear: NON-EU: €22,250 per academic year for Master of Arts programmes, INCLUDING regional tax (2026/27). One-year Academic Master, non-EU: €23,800. EU/EFTA by contrast is income-banded from €10,550 (ISEE up to €45,000) to €21,850 (over €150,000) for the MA, and €19,300 for the Academic Master. THE NON-EU PREMIUM IS THE HEADLINE ISSUE: he pays roughly DOUBLE the lowest EU band.
programs.tuitionTotal: €44,500 for the two-year Master of Arts as a non-EU student (2 × €22,250, 2026/27 rates). €23,800 for a one-year Academic Master.
programs.otherFees: Regional tax is stated to be INCLUDED in the €22,250 non-EU figure. However NABA separately states that Regional Tax for Academic Studies and the Graduation Thesis Fee are NOT included in scholarship amounts — i.e. a scholarship will not cover them. Enrolment fee, application fee and materials fees: UNVERIFIED on the pages read. NABA uses Flywire for international payments.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED on pages read.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €44,500 tuition over two years as a non-EU student, plus enrolment/thesis fees (UNVERIFIED), plus Milan living costs. Before scholarships, budget €60,000–70,000 over two years including living costs in Milan.
programs.scholarships: THIS IS THE STRONGEST SCHOLARSHIP PICTURE IN THE WHOLE SLICE FOR A NON-EU APPLICANT. (1) INTERNATIONAL POSTGRADUATE SCHOLARSHIP (portfolio-based): partial tuition coverage of €2,200 to €6,000 depending on category and income bracket, with NON-EU students in the highest bracket receiving UP TO €6,000; open to international students holding a degree (or obtaining one by end of 2025/26) with B1.2 English or Italian; assessed by faculty and admissions jury with particular weight on the PORTFOLIO; RENEWABLE for the second year if conditions are met; applies to BOTH Master of Arts and one-year Academic Master programmes at Milan and Rome starting October 2026; deadline 27 May 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm the 2027 date). For a February 2027 start the deadline is 25 September 2026. Awardees must enrol within 7 days of notification or forfeit. Note that separately NABA's MA-level award is quoted at up to €7,000 by income bracket. (2) EARLY ENROLMENT SCHOLARSHIP: 10% reduction on tuition for programmes starting October 2026, for international students and new registrations only (those who previously registered and postponed are excluded), applied automatically on enrolling by 29 January 2026 — no separate application. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm the 2027 equivalent. (3) FORMER NABA STUDENTS: 20% reduction on total tuition, excluding regional tax — not applicable to him. (4) DSU REGIONAL SCHOLARSHIP — see the dedicated Italy DSU entry; NABA administers it and non-EU students CAN apply, but for 2025/26 NABA Milan put only ONE scholarship to competition for 1st-year second-level students (and one at Rome), which makes it a lottery.
programs.paymentPlans: NABA partners with Flywire for international payments. Instalment structure and enrolment-fee schedule: UNVERIFIED on the pages read — request the payment schedule in writing. DSU scholarship money, when awarded, is paid in two instalments (around February and July/September) and the enrolment quota is reimbursed to winners, but tuition and academic contribution must still be paid in full first.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — MIUR/MUR-recognised AFAM institution. The Master of Arts is a Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello (120 ECTS), recognised by the Ministry and equivalent to a laurea magistrale for public competitions and doctoral/specialisation admission in artistic and musical fields; credits are valid in foreign university systems. WARNING: NABA's one-year 'Academic Master' programmes are Master universitario-type post-degree certificates and are NOT equivalent to a laurea magistrale — do not confuse the two.
programs.visaEligible: YES. NABA runs the full non-EU pipeline: UniversItaly pre-enrolment (normally March–November), passport/diploma/transcript/language upload, dichiarazione di valore or CIMEA attestation, and it warns the study visa typically takes 90 days. This is a well-trodden non-EU route.
programs.applicationOpens: UniversItaly pre-enrolment normally opens March and runs to November. International scholarship competition deadline 27 May 2026 for October 2026 entry; 25 September 2026 for February 2027 entry. Early Enrolment 10% discount required enrolling by 29 January 2026. ALL PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027 dates.
programs.deadline: 27 May 2026 (international scholarship, October 2026 entry) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for October 2027.
programs.reputationSignals: NABA is one of Italy's best-known private art academies, inside the state AFAM system, with Milan and Rome campuses and a genuinely international student body. Positive: transparent published fee brackets, a real non-EU-eligible scholarship, and a clear visa pipeline. RED FLAGS: the non-EU fee is roughly double the lowest EU band; no dedicated music-production or sound-engineering MA exists; and DSU competition numbers at second level are tiny (1 scholarship per campus per year band in 2025/26).
programs.recommendation: On money and process, NABA is the best-run non-EU option in this slice: it publishes real numbers, its scholarship explicitly names non-EU students and pays up to €6,000 renewable, and it stacks a 10% early-enrolment discount on top. Realistic best case: €22,250 − €6,000 − ~€2,225 = about €14,000 in year one, which is genuinely competitive against Berklee. BUT the subject fit is the problem — there is no music-production MA here, only digital/live performance and creative media production. Only pursue NABA if he is willing to reframe his goal towards performance technology and media production. If he does apply, apply EARLY (the 10% discount has a January deadline months before the scholarship deadline) and put everything into the portfolio, because the scholarship is portfolio-judged.

programs.scholarships: THIS ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE IED'S DSU BANDO IS THE CLEAREST PUBLISHED PROOF THAT A NON-EU STUDENT AT AN ITALIAN PRIVATE ACADEMY CAN WIN REGIONAL STATE AID. Key provisions of the Bando DSU 2025/26 (BAN 8203 rev 06, 4 September 2025), total fund €354,392.15 from MUR and Regione Lombardia: ELIGIBILITY expressly includes 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' alongside Italians and EU citizens, for students admitted or enrolled on a Diploma Accademico di Primo or Secondo Livello at Milan, Rome, Turin, Cagliari or Florence. INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario must not exceed €26,516.70 AND ISPE must not exceed €57,645.03 — both jointly. MERIT for a 1st-year II livello student: simply be regularly enrolled by 31 October and hold the first-level title by 31 January; confirmation of the full benefit then requires 40 credits by 10 August. AMOUNTS (including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; FUORI SEDE €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776. THE DECISIVE DETAIL: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, NON-EU FOREIGN STUDENTS ARE AUTOMATICALLY CLASSIFIED 'FUORI SEDE' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided the accommodation is paid for — so a Tunisian student is placed in the HIGHEST bracket, €5,776 to €8,134 per year. NON-EU DOCUMENTATION: an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' is required, built from foreign family-composition certificate, income declarations from the official tax agency of the country of residence (employer documents are NOT accepted, self-certification is NOT accepted), property and movable-asset statements, all translated into Italian by a recognised translator and legalised; Tunisia is NOT on the exemption or Apostille list published in the bando, so full consular legalisation applies. A floor applies: non-EU students' declared income cannot be counted below €7,002.97/year (the visa subsistence minimum). Free ISEEU assistance is via CAAF CGIL Lombardia under an IED agreement. DEADLINES 2025/26: applications 9 September to 7 November 2025; rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025. EXCLUSIONS THAT MATTER: anyone already holding an equal or higher qualification is excluded (a BSc does not block a II livello application); anyone receiving another income/merit-based grant for the same year is excluded; FOUNDATION course students are excluded; and the bando covers ONLY Diploma Accademico I/II livello — IED's one-year 'Master' courses are NOT covered. IED separately runs a commercial scholarship competition: 114 scholarships/tutorships covering 50% of tuition for Master of Arts and Master programmes 2025/26 across Italian campuses and Accademia di Como, rising to 127 for 2026/27 across Italy and Spain, open to local and international students including non-EU, covering partial tuition only and NOT living costs or enrolment fees.
programs.paymentPlans: UNVERIFIED — not published in the DSU bando. Note that DSU is not a fee waiver: 'Le tasse di iscrizione e di contributo accademico dovranno comunque essere interamente versate' — fees must be paid in full and the scholarship arrives afterwards, in instalments.

Lombardia 33/2004 and DPCM 9/4/2001 for right-to-study purposes). Also note IED's dedicated SOUND DESIGN programme is a FIRST-level diploma (BA equivalent), not a master.
programs.visaEligible: Yes for the Diploma Accademico route — the bando references 'permesso di soggiorno' for extra-EU students as a routine document, and the visa subsistence figure of €7,002.97 is built into the income rules, confirming this is a standard non-EU pathway.

programs.deadline: DSU application deadline 7 November 2025; rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.reputationSignals: IED is a major international private design chain with campuses across Italy, Spain and Brazil, operating inside the AFAM system, with a substantial published DSU fund (€354,392.15 for 2025/26) and a formal CAAF agreement to help foreign students obtain the ISEE parificato. RED FLAGS for this candidate: no second-level sound-design or music-production programme (Sound Design is BA-level only), tuition not published, and the DSU documentation burden for a Tunisian is heavy — consular-legalised tax documents from the Tunisian revenue authority, translated into Italian.
programs.recommendation: IED itself does not offer what he wants at master level — its Sound Design programme is an undergraduate diploma. Include IED in his research NOT as a destination but as the clearest published evidence of how the Italian DSU route works for a non-EU student: he can win €5,776–€8,134 a year at an Italian PRIVATE academy because non-EU students are automatically classed 'fuori sede'. Use that same mechanism at NABA, RUFA or Saint Louis instead. Practical warning: start collecting the Tunisian tax and property certificates, translations and legalisations at least four months before the September/November DSU window — self-certification is refused outright and employer letters are not accepted.

On a 10-month billing year that is approximately €3,654 per year. INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS PAY THE SAME TUITION TABLE AS EVERYONE ELSE — Lusófona states foreign/international students 'beneficiam da mesma tabela de propinas (mensalidades) que todos os outros estudantes'. There is NO non-EU surcharge on tuition.
programs.tuitionTotal: Approximately €7,308 for the full 120-ECTS master (2 years at €3,654/year, 2025/26 rates). At €12.18 per ECTS × 120 ECTS = €1,461.60 per 30-ECTS semester block, the arithmetic supports roughly €7,300 total. CONFIRM the 2027/28 table.
programs.otherFees: Application fee (candidatura) €450; enrolment/registration (inscrição/matrícula) €300; school insurance (seguro escolar) €47 — 2025/26 figures. Note the application-fee rule: if the candidate holds a non-EU nationality and has not resided in Portugal continuously for more than two years as at 1 January of the entry year, the FOREIGN-CANDIDATE application fee applies under the emoluments order in force — so the €450 is the non-EU rate. Materials, exam and equipment fees: UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Software focus is Avid Pro Tools, Max/MSP and Arduino. Whether licences must be bought personally: UNVERIFIED — Pro Tools and Max are commercial licences and student versions are typically required. Budget for these separately.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Year one: €450 application + €300 enrolment + €47 insurance + ~€3,654 tuition = approximately €4,451. Two-year programme total roughly €8,100 in fees, plus Lisbon living costs of about €9,000–12,000 per year. All-in two-year estimate: €27,000–33,000 — by far the cheapest accredited master's in this entire slice, roughly one-eighth the cost of Berklee Valencia.
programs.scholarships: NO INSTITUTIONAL SCHOLARSHIP IS PUBLISHED on the pages read for this programme, and the national scheme is CLOSED TO HIM. Portuguese DGES bolsas de ação social direta require Portuguese nationality, or foreign nationality with a PERMANENT residence permit in Portugal, or coverage by a cooperation agreement, or reciprocity, or stateless/refugee status. Under Decreto-Lei 36/2014 as amended by Decreto-Lei 62/2018, 'estudantes internacionais' benefit ONLY from indirect social action (canteens, facilities) — they are EXCLUDED from the direct monetary grant. The one exception is students granted humanitarian-emergency status, who receive both direct and indirect support. DGES does note that some private higher-education institutions offer their own bolsas to economically disadvantaged students whose nationality is not covered by the DGES scheme — i.e. all foreign students without a residence title — so it is worth ASKING Lusófona directly whether such an internal fund exists for this programme. Status: UNVERIFIED. Erasmus+ mobility funding may be available once enrolled, but it is not entry funding.
programs.paymentPlans: MONTHLY BY DEFAULT — this is the key financial advantage. Tuition is billed as mensalidades due by the 8th of each month. International/foreign students must settle the FIRST TWO MONTHLY INSTALMENTS at the moment of matrícula/inscrição (Ordem de Serviço nº 8/2019). So the up-front outlay at enrolment is application €450 + inscrição/matrícula €300 + seguro €47 + 2 × €365.40 = approximately €1,527. Payment methods: credit card and PayPal online; Multibanco or cash in person. No interest or finance charge is mentioned — this is a genuine instalment arrangement, not a loan, which contrasts sharply with microFusa's 8.95% APR scheme in Spain.
programs.accreditationStatus: OFFICIAL — A3ES status 'Acreditado', registration R/A-Cr 34/2018/AL01. This is a full second-cycle mestrado, not a pós-graduação. Universidade Lusófona is a private university operating within the Portuguese higher-education system with DGES/A3ES oversight.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an A3ES-accredited mestrado at a recognised private university is a standard basis for a Portuguese student residence visa, and Lusófona operates a dedicated international-student admissions channel with its own fee schedule for foreign candidates. Confirm the specific documentation with SIGA (siga@ulusofona.pt). Status for this programme specifically: UNVERIFIED as an entitlement but strongly supported by the institutional set-up.

programs.reputationSignals: A3ES-accredited with a published registration number; a genuinely technical, hands-on curriculum (acoustics, synthesis, Max/MSP, Arduino, studio practice) that maps unusually well onto a software-engineering background; evening/post-work delivery from 6pm, which leaves daytime free for studio work or a job. RED FLAGS: taught entirely in Portuguese; no published scholarship; the €450 application fee is high for Portugal and is non-refundable; and Portuguese national social-action grants are closed to international students.
programs.recommendation: THIS IS THE STRONGEST VALUE PROPOSITION IN THE ENTIRE SLICE and the one he should look at hardest. An A3ES-ACCREDITED master's — a real degree, not a certificate — in exactly his subject, at a private university, for roughly €7,300 in tuition over two years, with monthly interest-free instalments and no non-EU tuition premium. The curriculum (acoustics, digital audio computing, synthesis, Max/MSP, Arduino) is arguably BETTER suited to a software engineer than any music-conservatory route, and the 75% portfolio-and-interview weighting means his portfolio matters more than his lack of a music degree. The one real obstacle is LANGUAGE: it is taught in Portuguese, and he has 13 months. If he is willing to commit to intensive Portuguese starting now, this is the best risk-adjusted choice available to him. Actions: (1) email the coordinator now to confirm the required Portuguese level and whether any English accommodation exists; (2) ask explicitly whether Lusófona operates an internal bolsa for international students outside the DGES scheme — DGES itself says some private institutions do; (3) budget €1,527 for the enrolment moment.

programs.scholarships: TWO ABSOLUTE EXCLUSIONS HE MUST UNDERSTAND BEFORE CHOOSING SPAIN. (1) TITLE-TYPE EXCLUSION: Becas MEC can be requested only for official undergraduate (grado) and OFFICIAL master's studies. They CANNOT be requested for a 'título propio' or a permanent-education programme. Third-cycle studies, specialisation studies and títulos propios are all outside the scheme. Fees must be paid to a Spanish centre. This alone kills MEC funding for Universidad Europea's Máster en Producción Creativa de la Música, TAI's Máster en Producción Musical, SAE Spain's UDIMA Máster de Formación Permanente, and every microFusa diploma. (2) NATIONALITY/RESIDENCE EXCLUSION: non-EU foreigners must hold LEGAL RESIDENCE ('residencia legal') in Spain to qualify. The situation of 'estancia' — which is exactly what a study authorisation confers — does NOT give any right to a university grant. Holding an authorisation of stay is expressly not sufficient. EU citizens must be permanent residents or prove employment. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded even if he chose an OFFICIAL master's. (3) COMUNIDAD DE MADRID: its student grants target students enrolled at MADRID PUBLIC universities on official grado or master's studies in disadvantaged socio-economic situations; and its Becas de Excelencia expressly EXCLUDE 'estudios de máster, especialización o títulos propios'. No Comunidad de Madrid route exists for a private-university título propio. (4) GENERALITAT DE CATALUNYA non-university grants (€300–350 basic, €50–125 performance, €1,700 income-based, €2,700 relocation, 2026-2027) are tied to Catalan income/academic and residence conditions and are not reachable by a newly arrived non-EU student. (5) WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN TO HIM IN SPAIN: only institution-level commercial discounts (early place-reservation, alumni, referral) and one genuinely nationality-blind private award found in this research — the YAMAHA MUSIC EUROPE FOUNDATION grant of €1,000–2,000 per year for students under 25 enrolled at a recognised European music institution, distributing roughly €66,000 a year.
programs.paymentPlans: Not applicable — but note the consequence: because no state aid reaches him, every Spanish private option must be financed entirely from savings, family, or a commercial instalment plan (which in the microFusa case carries 8.95% APR and requires a Spanish bank account he cannot open before arrival).
programs.accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL / NOT APPLICABLE — this entry documents an exclusion rule, not a programme.
programs.visaEligible: Not applicable, but the interaction is the key insight: the very visa status that lets him study in Spain ('estancia por estudios') is the status that disqualifies him from Spanish state grants.
programs.applicationOpens: Annual call, normally spring. Not relevant to him given the exclusions.
programs.deadline: Not relevant given the exclusions. PRIOR CYCLE dates not tracked.
programs.reputationSignals: This is the single most important structural finding for Spain: the country with the most heavily marketed private 'másteres' in music production is also the country where none of them attracts state support for a non-EU student.
programs.recommendation: Treat Spain as a FULLY SELF-FUNDED market. There is no scenario in which a Tunisian on a study visa receives Spanish state or regional aid for a private-sector music-production programme — he fails the title-type test and the residence test independently. Therefore: (a) ignore any school that gestures vaguely at 'becas del ministerio'; (b) judge Spanish options purely on sticker price minus the school's own commercial discount; (c) if he is under 25, apply to the Yamaha Music Europe Foundation, which is the only nationality-blind award found; and (d) always ask the school in writing whether the programme is a 'Máster Universitario Oficial' or a 'Título Propio / Máster de Formación Permanente' — and get the answer in an email, not a phone call.

programs.scholarships: THE DECISIVE MECHANISM: NON-EU STUDENTS ARE ELIGIBLE, AND THEY LAND IN THE HIGHEST-VALUE BRACKET. (1) ELIGIBILITY: the IED bando states plainly that applications may be made by Italian citizens, EU citizens, AND 'i cittadini di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea' (under DPR 394/1999 arts. 44-bis and 46(5), and D.lgs 286/1998). Non-EU students at a PRIVATE academy are explicitly in scope. (2) THE 'FUORI SEDE' RULE: under Art. 13(3) DPCM 9/4/2001, non-EU foreign students are AUTOMATICALLY treated as 'fuori sede' regardless of where they live in Italy (unless their family lives in Italy), provided they pay for accommodation. Fuori sede is the top payment band. (3) AMOUNTS (IED, Lombardy, 2025/26, including €140 regional-tax reimbursement and €818 meal allowance): fuori sede €8,134 / €7,073 / €5,776 by income band 1/2/3; pendolari €4,754 / €4,134 / €3,254; in sede €3,383 / €2,950 / €2,114. NABA quotes a range of roughly €2,000 to €8,000 including a free daily meal. So a Tunisian student renting a room in Milan is looking at €5,776–€8,134 per year. (4) INCOME TEST: ISEE Universitario ≤ €26,516.70 AND ISPE ≤ €57,645.03 — both must be satisfied. Income bands: 1st €0–13,258.35; 2nd €13,258.36–17,677.80; 3rd €17,677.81–26,516.70. (5) MERIT FOR A FIRST-YEAR SECOND-LEVEL STUDENT: essentially just enrolment plus holding the first-level title; full confirmation then requires 38–40 credits by the following 10 August. (6) THE NON-EU PAPERWORK — THIS IS THE HARD PART: he needs an 'ISEEU-ISPEU parificato' built from (a) a certificate of current foreign household composition, (b) income declarations for each household member for the reference calendar year issued by the OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT TAX AGENCY of the country of residence — employer documents are expressly NOT accepted and self-certification is expressly NOT valid, (c) property holdings with square metres or a certificate of no property for every member aged 18+, (d) movable assets (securities, dividends, shareholdings, company net-worth fractions, accounts). Everything must be translated into Italian by a recognised translator and LEGALISED. TUNISIA IS NOT on the bando's legalisation-exemption list and NOT on the Apostille list — so full consular legalisation applies. A floor also applies: non-EU declared income cannot be treated as below €7,002.97/year, the visa subsistence minimum. IED has a convention with CAAF CGIL Lombardia to help foreign students obtain the parificato. (7) COMPETITION IS THE RISK: for 2025/26 NABA Milano put just ONE scholarship to competition for first-year second-level students (and one at NABA Roma); IED pooled €354,392.15 across four ranking lists proportional to applicant numbers. Ranking for first-year students is purely a function of ISEE — a lower ISEE ranks higher. (8) INCOMPATIBILITY: receiving any other income- or merit-based grant for the same year is an automatic exclusion, so DSU cannot be stacked with the institution's own scholarship. (9) PAYMENT: two instalments (roughly February and July/September); second-assignment winners get one payment around December. Paid ONLY by bank transfer to an Italian or SEPA account in the student's name — he will need a European bank account.
programs.paymentPlans: Not applicable. Note the cash-flow trap: fees must be paid in full BEFORE the scholarship is awarded, and the first instalment does not arrive until around February. He must be able to fund the whole first term unaided.
programs.accreditationStatus: Applies ONLY to Diploma Accademico di PRIMO or SECONDO livello courses. It does NOT apply to one-year 'Master' courses at IED, and Foundation-course students are excluded. This is another reason to choose a biennio (II livello) over a 'Master di I livello'.
programs.visaEligible: Not applicable directly, but the scheme presupposes a valid permesso di soggiorno for extra-EU students and builds the €7,002.97 visa subsistence minimum into its income rules — confirming it is designed for genuine non-EU students.
programs.applicationOpens: IED 2025/26: applications from 9 September 2025. NABA 2025/26: online form by 22 September 2025. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027/28 dates (expect early September 2027).
programs.deadline: IED 7 November 2025 (rent contract for fuori sede status by 10 December 2025); NABA 22 September 2025 online / 25 September 2025 documents. Provisional rankings by 31 October, appeals within 15 days, final rankings by 30 November. ALL PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.reputationSignals: This is genuine public money (MUR plus regional funds) flowing to students at PRIVATE academies — an arrangement that has no equivalent in Spain, Portugal or the Netherlands for a non-EU student. IED alone put €354,392.15 to competition for 2025/26. RED FLAGS: brutal documentation requirements for a Tunisian; very small numbers of second-level awards at some campuses; no automatic renewal; and the cash arrives months after fees are due.
programs.recommendation: THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINANCIAL FINDING FOR HIM. Italy is the only one of the four countries where a Tunisian studying at a PRIVATE institution can receive substantial state-backed money — €5,776 to €8,134 a year, because non-EU students are automatically classed 'fuori sede'. Combined with a NABA international scholarship (up to €6,000) — though note the two are INCOMPATIBLE and he must choose — or with Saint Louis's much lower fees, this changes the economics completely. Concrete actions, starting NOW and not in 2027: (1) obtain official Tunisian tax-authority income statements for the whole household for the relevant year, plus property and asset certificates, plus a household-composition certificate; (2) get them translated into Italian by a recognised translator and fully consular-legalised — Tunisia has no Apostille shortcut here; (3) plan to have a registered rental contract in Italy by early December of the entry year, or he is downgraded from fuori sede to pendolare and loses €2,000–4,000; (4) budget to pay the entire first term of fees before any scholarship money arrives; (5) open a SEPA bank account early, since payment is by transfer only.

programs.scholarships: THE SCHEME: €5,000, paid in the FIRST YEAR of study only. It is expressly 'not a full-tuition scholarship'. THE EXCLUSION: for the 2026-2027 academic year the participating institutions number 11 research universities and 24 universities of applied sciences — all PUBLICLY FUNDED (bekostigd) Dutch institutions. Private, non-government-funded (niet-bekostigd) institutions are NOT identified as participating. Consequently a non-EEA student enrolling at SAE Institute Amsterdam, Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam, Dutch Dance Music Academy, Sound Education Nederland, Music Production Academy, Pro Audio Education NL or any comparable private audio provider CANNOT access the NL Scholarship. Deadlines are set individually by each participating institution — irrelevant to him since none of the relevant audio providers participates. Separately, Dutch studiefinanciering and DUO student loans do not reach non-EEA students at private providers; Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states outright that because it is a private institute its students are not eligible for a visa or a student loan.

programs.visaEligible: Not applicable directly, but the same bekostigd/niet-bekostigd divide that closes the scholarship also drives visa sponsorship: a Dutch study residence permit requires an IND recognised sponsor (erkend referent) and an accredited programme. Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam explicitly cannot sponsor non-EU students; SAE Amsterdam is silent on the question on its public pages (UNVERIFIED).

programs.deadline: Set individually by each participating institution — typically February to May. Not reachable through any private audio provider.
programs.reputationSignals: A well-run, well-known national scheme — which makes its inapplicability here all the more decisive. It is worth noting the mirror image: if he were willing to consider a PUBLIC Dutch institution (out of scope for this brief), the €5,000 NL Scholarship would open up.
programs.recommendation: On the funding evidence, DROP THE NETHERLANDS from the private-sector shortlist. The €5,000 NL Scholarship cannot follow him to a private institution; Dutch student loans cannot either; SAE Amsterdam publishes no scholarships at all and stays silent on visa sponsorship; and Abbey Road Institute Amsterdam states in writing that it cannot help a non-EU resident get a visa. That combination — highest living costs of the four countries, zero funding, and an unresolved or negative visa position — makes the Dutch private sector the worst value in this slice for a Tunisian national. Amsterdam remains the right city for his career; it is simply not accessible to him through a private school. Revisit only if a public Dutch institution comes into scope.

programs.scholarships: THE RULE: to apply for a DGES bolsa de estudo, a candidate must hold Portuguese nationality; OR foreign nationality WITH a PERMANENT residence permit in Portugal; OR be covered by cooperation agreements providing such benefits; OR be a national of a state whose law grants equal treatment to Portuguese students in equal circumstances; OR be stateless or hold political refugee status. THE EXCLUSION: students admitted under 'estudante internacional' status benefit EXCLUSIVELY from INDIRECT social action under Decreto-Lei n.º 36/2014 of 10 March, as amended by Decreto-Lei n.º 62/2018 of 6 August — meaning canteens, facilities and services, but NOT the direct monetary grant. A Tunisian arriving on a study visa is therefore excluded from DGES cash support at BOTH public and private institutions. THE ONE EXCEPTION: international students granted 'estudante em situação de emergência por razões humanitárias' status receive the full range of direct and indirect support — not applicable to him. THE IMPORTANT SILVER LINING, STATED BY DGES ITSELF: some PRIVATE higher-education institutions offer their own bolsas to economically disadvantaged students whose nationality is not covered by the DGES scheme — that is, precisely all foreign students without a residence title. This is the door he should push on. Concrete examples found in this research: UCP Porto grants scholarships annually to candidates of non-Portuguese nationality who do NOT reside in Portugal, giving partial exemption from the master's tuition, awarded on application average plus interview (contact ee.bolsas@ucp.pt); UCP's Escola das Artes runs Bolsas de Mérito e Incentivo à Investigação for master's students giving total or partial tuition exemption; and The Social Hub Changemaker Housing Scholarship targets refugee and international students. Lusófona publishes no equivalent on the pages read (UNVERIFIED — ask).
programs.paymentPlans: Not applicable — but note that Portuguese private universities structure tuition as interest-free MONTHLY instalments (Lusófona €365.40/month, UCP €657/month), which is a materially better cash-flow deal than Spain's interest-bearing plans or the Netherlands' instalment premiums. Lusófona requires international students to pay the first TWO monthly instalments at matrícula.
programs.accreditationStatus: Not applicable — but the parallel Portuguese trap is the mestrado/pós-graduação distinction: a 'mestrado' accredited by A3ES is a degree; a 'pós-graduação' is a post-graduate COURSE that is not a degree. ETIC's offerings are neither.
programs.visaEligible: Not applicable directly. Note that DGES also administers the 'Concurso Especial para Estudantes Internacionais', the special admission route for international students — the same status that grants admission is the status that removes grant eligibility.
programs.applicationOpens: Annual, normally summer (the 2025/2026 call opened in the summer of 2025). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027/28 dates. Not relevant to him given the exclusion.
programs.deadline: Set annually by DGES. Not relevant given the exclusion.
programs.reputationSignals: Portugal is the cheapest of the four countries for accredited private master's study by a very wide margin (Lusófona ~€7,300 total tuition; UCP Porto €13,140 total), which substantially offsets the absence of national grant access. The exclusion hurts far less here than it would in Spain.
programs.recommendation: Understand the split clearly: Portuguese NATIONAL money is closed to him, but Portuguese PRIVATE INSTITUTIONAL money is not, and DGES says so explicitly. So in Portugal he should stop looking at government schemes entirely and instead write directly to institutional scholarship offices. The highest-value single action in this whole slice is to email ee.bolsas@ucp.pt and ask for the regulation and the amount of the scholarship for non-Portuguese nationals not resident in Portugal — that award is designed for his exact profile. Then ask Lusófona the same question. Combined with tuition of €3,654/year (Lusófona) or €6,570/year (UCP Porto) paid interest-free monthly, Portugal is the only country in this slice where a self-funding Tunisian can realistically complete an ACCREDITED master's in sound without debt.

Evidence: (a) ESIC's own master index at esic.edu was fetched and lists only business, marketing, digital marketing, big data, logistics, finance, project management, HR and international trade — no music, sound, audio or audiovisual production programme of any kind, at either the oficial or the título propio tier. The two nearest UIC items are the Máster Universitario en Gestión Cultural (Arts and Cultural Management — an OFICIAL humanities master) and the Postgraduate Degree in Management of Cultural and Creative Industries; both are arts-MANAGEMENT/administration programmes that touch the music industry as a sector to be managed. Neither teaches production, mixing, sound design or live electronics, and neither would give him studio hours, a portfolio or DJ/producer craft. They are the wrong instrument for his goal and should not be treated as substitutes. (c) Universidad Villanueva's master catalogue was fetched: MBA, marketing digital, HR, risk prevention, LLM, tax, abogacía, teacher training, psychopedagogy, ed-tech, several psychology masters, sports journalism and event management. Its only audiovisual offering is the undergraduate Grado en Comunicación Audiovisual — a bachelor, and a general audiovisual-communication one at that, not music production. He already holds a bachelor, so it is doubly irrelevant. Rule all three out and spend no further time on them. Related negative finding, also verified: Universidad Loyola (private, Seville/Dos Hermanas and Córdoba) does run a Creación y Producción Musical programme with the University of San Francisco, and it is genuinely production-focused and portfolio-driven — but it is a GRADO PROPIO, i.e. a BACHELOR-level qualification AND the university's own title rather than an ANECA-official grado. It is out of scope on both counts for a graduate seeking a September 2027 master. The practical takeaway for this slice: mainstream Spanish private universities do not serve music production at master level. The real Spanish options for him sit either in specialist audio academies (SAE Madrid/Barcelona, Microfusa, TAI) — which mostly issue títulos propios with the visa caveat above — or in public universities (notably UPF Barcelona's Máster en Tecnologías del Sonido y de la Música, which is ANECA-official but heavily engineering/research-oriented rather than DJ/producer craft). programs.recommendation: AVOID as a route to becoming a DJ/producer — the decisive reason is that it teaches none of the craft he asked for. Nine months and (probably) five figures buy him concert logistics, contracts, ticketing and sponsorship; he would not touch a DAW, a console or a studio. Two further problems compound it: the award is a título propio, so he would pay master-level money for a school certificate with no ANECA verification, no EHEA recognition and no PhD access; and UAX publishes no price at all, which for a budget-sensitive self-payer is disqualifying on its own — never commit to a programme that will not tell you what it costs. FLAG IT TO HIM ANYWAY, honestly, as a strategic alternative, because it solves the two problems no production school solves for him: it needs no portfolio and no musicianship proof, so his admissions weaknesses vanish; and the Live Nation, Ticketmaster, Superstruct and Mad Cool relationships are the most commercially valuable industry links anywhere in this Spanish slice, with faculty drawn from the Pacha/Woomoon/Ibiza electronic economy. If his true goal is "work in international electronic music" rather than "be the person at the desk", this is a real door — and his software-engineering degree is a genuine asset in ticketing and music-data roles. Two hard conditions before he would ever consider it: get the total non-EU price in writing, and get written confirmation that UAX will issue a carta de admisión supporting a student visa for a título propio. Also note he would be studying negotiation and contract law in Spanish, which without B2 Spanish is not survivable. If the official-degree route matters to him more than the subject, the sister Máster Universitario en Gestión de la Cultura, el Deporte, los Medios y el Entretenimiento (Málaga) is the one genuinely ANECA-official title in this family.
